title: CLCON/406/2020 of MAHESH MALIK Vs JAGMOHAN SINGH CHAUHAN

paras.text:
CLCON No. 406 of 2020
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Apparently, as per the pleadings which has
been raised in the contempt, which has been
placed before this Court, the petitioner claims that
a lease was granted to him on the land belonging
to the Irrigation Department in the year 1990
initially for 10 years initially, which was
extendable to a maximum period of 30 years, it
was an admitted case that the lease was never
renewed, thereafter. During the intervening period
a PIL was preferred before this Court being PIL
No.47 of 2013, Manmohan Lakhera vs. State of
Uttarakhand and others, whereby the Division
Bench of this Court vide its judgment dated
18.06.2018, issued certain directions to be
adhered to for the purpose of removing the
unauthorised constructions. Aggrieved against the
said judgment, the one namely Sunita, had
approached the Hon'ble Apex Court by way of a
SLP (Civil) No.24083 of 2018, which was
decided by the Hon'ble Apex Court, by the
judgment of 04.07.2018, modifying the directions
as contained therein by Division Bench limited to
the extent of resorting to the process of removing
of unauthorised occupants and had laid down
certain parameters for issuing a prior show cause
notice, before making any efforts for removing
the unauthorised encroachment, as directed by the
Division Bench by the judgment dated
18.06.2018.
Petitioner had filed a writ petition, being
Writ Petition No.1854 of 2018, Suresh Vervani
and others vs. Chief Engineer Public Works
Department. The petitioner's Writ Petition was
dismissed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court
by the judgment dated 29.06.2018, which was put
to challenge by the petitioner in a special appeal,
being Special Appeal No.514 of 2018, which too

was decided by the Division Bench by the
judgment of 13.07.2018, in the light of the
judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court dated
04.07.2018.
The grievance of the petitioner is that,
despite of, the directions given by the Hon'ble
Apex Court in its judgment dated 04.07.2018, for
issuance of a prior notice, the respondents have
not adhered to it and, hence, they have violated
the judgments which laid down the parameters to
be adopted for resorting to an anti encroachment
drive as directed by the Division Bench judgment
dated 18.06.2018, hence, he submits that the
entire action of the respondents happens to be in
contravention to the aforesaid judgments, hence,
the contempt. A reference may be had to the
pleadings raised in para 6 of the Contempt
Petition which is quoted hereunder:
"that since 13.07.2018 till today no notice
was served upon the petitioner an suddenly again
on 21.07.2018 contemnor along with there team
approached the Dilaram Bazar and marked the
shops as encroachment and thus immediately
again the petitioner send the copy of order through
registered post on 21.10.2020 which was received
by contemnors on 22.10.2020 as traced by tracking
report. A true copy of postal receipts is annexed as
Annexure No.5 to this affidavit."
The pleadings as per the para 6 reflects that
the grievance of the petitioner is that action of
respondent was averse of the judgment as was
rendered by the Division Bench of 13.07.2018, no
notice was ever served upon him and again, the
respondents had appeared on 21.07.2018, along
with the team too and mark the shops as
encroachment as thus alleged to have been made
on the land of the Irrigation Department. Meaning
thereby, the knowledge of an action which was to
be taken in pursuance to the judgments referred
above was brought to the knowledge of the
petitioner on 21.07.2018, as per his own
pleadings, but, he never proceeded to take any
action of the institution to an appropriate

contempt proceedings and according to his own
case also after the said action on 21.07.2018, he
had issued notices to the respondent for the first
time by registered post on 21.10.2020.
His grievance is that despite of the said
notice being sent his shop was demolished on
24.10.2020. Apparently, the action of removing
the encroachment as per the pleadings, was
initiated on 21.07.2018, and it was that point of
time rather the petitioner ought to have
approached the Contempt Court, if at all, there
was any dereliction of the judgment and directions
already issued by the Writ Court as well as by the
Hon'ble Apex Court. When the action taken and
was initiated on 21.07.2018, he himself has
reacted to it for the first time on 21.10.2020, and
then filling of contempt now on 02.11.2020,
alleging non-compliance of the judgment on
13.07.2018, would be apparently barred by
Section 20 of the Contempt of Courts Act.
In view of the aforesaid, since, the period
prescribed under the Act, itself, has expired for
initiating the contempt, this Contempt Petition is
prima facie barred under Section 20 of the
Contempt of Courts Act, hence, the same is
accordingly dismissed.
